request.spec:
Show a due-total per calendar month: for every month (yyyy-mm) that any claim on the sheet is
dated in, the due of the claims dated in that month that count.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
Show a due-total per calendar month: for every month (yyyy-mm) that any claim on the sheet is
dated in, the due of the claims dated in that month that count.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
The sheet now shows a due-total for each calendar month, and all 4 tests in `bin/e2e` pass.

There's one line per month (yyyy-mm) that any claim on the sheet is dated in, oldest month first. Each shows the total due of the claims dated in that month that count, labelled `month-<yyyy-mm>-due-total`. A month whose claims don't count still appears, with `0.00`. When the sheet has no claims, the list doesn't appear at all.

It works the same way as the existing per-tag due-totals: the screen works it out from data it already loads, using the same rules for which claims count and the same due calculation. So I didn't need to change the stored data, the server or the audit file.

The change is two new files in `src/main/frontend/features/months/`:
- **`MonthTotals.tsx`**: works out and shows the monthly totals.
- **`months.slot.tsx`**: adds that list to the main screen, just after the tag totals.
